HDFS-16286.title: Debug tool to verify the correctness of erasure coding on file
HDFS-16286.description:
Block data in erasure coded block group may corrupt and the block meta (checksum) is unable to discover the corruption in some cases such as EC reconstruction, related issues are:  HDFS-14768, HDFS-15186, HDFS-15240.

In addition to HDFS-15759, there needs a tool to check erasure coded file whether any block group has data corruption in case of other conditions rather than EC reconstruction, or the feature HDFS-15759(validation during EC reconstruction) is not open(which is close by default now).

commits.message: Add a debug tool to verify the correctness of erasure coding on file
commits.author: cndaimin

commits.message: Fix review comments and add unit test
commits.author: cndaimin

HDFS-16266.title: Add remote port information to HDFS audit log
HDFS-16266.description:
In our production environment, we occasionally encounter a problem where a user submits an abnormal computation task, causing a sudden flood of requests, which causes the queueTime and processingTime of the Namenode to rise very high, causing a large backlog of tasks.

We usually locate and kill specific Spark, Flink, or MapReduce tasks based on metrics and audit logs. Currently, IP and UGI are recorded in audit logs, but there is no port information, so it is difficult to locate specific processes sometimes. Therefore, I propose that we add the port information to the audit log, so that we can easily track the upstream process.

Currently, some projects contain port information in audit logs, such as Hbase and Alluxio. I think it is also necessary to add port information for HDFS audit logs.

commits.message: HDFS-16266. Add remote port information to HDFS audit log
commits.author: tomscut

HDFS-16320.title: Datanode retrieve slownode information from NameNode
HDFS-16320.description:
The current information of slownode is reported by reportingNode, and stored in NameNode.

This ticket is to let the slownode retrieve the information from NameNode, so that it can do other performance improvement actions based on this information.

commits.message: HDFS-16320. Datanode retrieve slownode information from NameNode
commits.author: symious

HDFS-16331.title: Make dfs.blockreport.intervalMsec reconfigurable
HDFS-16331.description:
We have a cold data cluster, which stores as EC policy. There are 24 fast disks on each node and each disk is 7 TB. 

Recently, many nodes have more than 10 million blocks, and the interval of FBR is 6h as default. Frequent FBR caused great pressure on NN.

!image-2021-11-18-09-35-35-400.png|width=334,height=229!

!image-2021-11-18-09-33-24-236.png|width=566,height=159!

We want to increase the interval of FBR, but have to rolling restart the DNs, this operation is very heavy. In this scenario, it is necessary to make _dfs.blockreport.intervalMsec_ reconfigurable.

HDFS-16327.title: Make dfs.namenode.max.slowpeer.collect.nodes reconfigurable
HDFS-16327.description:
As the HDFS cluster expands or shrinks, the number of slow nodes to be filtered must be dynamically adjusted. So we should make DFS_NAMENODE_MAX_SLOWPEER_COLLECT_NODES_KEY reconfigurable.

See HDFS-15879.

HDFS-16386.title: Reduce DataNode load when FsDatasetAsyncDiskService is working
HDFS-16386.description:
Our DataNode node has 36 disks. When FsDatasetAsyncDiskService is working, it will cause a high load on the DataNode.
Here are some monitoring related to memory:
 !monitor.png! 
Since each disk deletes the block asynchronously, and each thread allows 4 threads to work,
This will cause some troubles to the DataNode, such as increased cpu and increased memory.
We should appropriately reduce the number of jobs of the total thread so that the DataNode can work better.

commits.message: HDFS-16386.Reduce DataNode load when FsDatasetAsyncDiskService is working.
commits.author: jianghuazhu
